title: Accepted for CPS, NEU
content:
Hey, Husky's

I got admission into CPS, NEU Boston campus for Spring intake. However, I haven't received the I-20 yet, I have raised a request in my graduation application portal but theres no response yet. Could someone please help me how to get the I-20? Should I submit my financial ability to OGS in order to get I-20? 

Also, regarding the stay. I request some help about the places/residential places to stay. Kindly, reach me out directly in dm or reply to this thread. Your help will be much appreciated.

comments.body:
Per Claude:

**1. Be admitted and confirm enrollment**  
After admission, the student must **accept/confirm enrollment** and complete the required items in Northeastern’s admissions portal. Northeastern generally requires any enrollment deposit to be paid before the I-20 request becomes available.   
**2. Request the I-20 through myOGS**  
Once eligible, the student accesses **myOGS** and submits the electronic **Initial I-20 Request**.  
The student generally uploads:  
Passport identification page  
Proof of sufficient financial resources for the program  
Currency conversion if financial documents aren’t in U.S. dollars  
Sponsor letter/affidavit if the sponsor is a non-blood relative  
The financial documentation must demonstrate funds sufficient for Northeastern’s estimated tuition/fees and living expenses.   
Northeastern’s current pre-arrival materials say **initial I-20 processing is approximately 15 business days**, although it can fluctuate during busy periods.   
**3. Northeastern issues the I-20**  
The I-20 is the university-issued **Certificate of Eligibility for F-1 status**. It contains the student’s SEVIS ID and program information.  
**The I-20 is not the F-1 visa.** The sequence is:  
**Northeastern admission → I-20 → SEVIS fee → DS-160 → visa interview → F-1 visa → travel to U.S.**  
Northeastern specifically lists this sequence on its current F-1 visa page.   
**4. Pay the I-901 SEVIS fee**  
After receiving the I-20, the student generally pays the **I-901 SEVIS fee**. A SEVIS transfer student generally doesn’t pay it again.   
**5. Complete the DS-160**  
The student completes the U.S. Department of State’s **DS-160 Online Nonimmigrant Visa Application** and pays the applicable visa application fee.  
Northeastern says the student should have the following available:  
I-20  
Passport  
SEVIS I-901 receipt  
Northeastern admission/acceptance letter  
Financial documentation  
DS-160 confirmation  
Required photograph   
**6. Schedule the F-1 visa interview**  
The student schedules an appointment with a U.S. embassy/consulate.  
**Important current rule:** Northeastern’s September 2026 guidance says that, since September 6, 2025, F/J visa applicants generally must schedule their interview in their **country of nationality or residence**.   
**7. Attend the interview**  
The consular officer decides whether to issue the F-1 visa. The student should be prepared to explain:  
Why Northeastern  
What program they will study  
How the education will be financed  
Their academic background  
Their plans after completing their studies  
Additional documentation can be requested, including academic records and evidence relevant to the student’s intent to depart the U.S. after the authorized period of study.   
**8. Receive the F-1 visa and travel**  
Once approved, the F-1 visa is placed in the passport.  
Northeastern says F-1 students can apply for the visa **up to 120 days before the I-20 program start date**.   
The student then travels to the U.S. with the required immigration documents, including the passport with F-1 visa and I-20.  
**9. Complete Northeastern’s immigration clearance after arrival**  
After arriving in the U.S., the student must complete Northeastern OGS’s **Online Immigration Clearance**. For a new student with an initial I-20, Northeastern currently requires this within **30 days of the program start date**. The student provides the passport, F-1 visa, I-94 and U.S. address.

For CPS Graduate programs, they list the following for financial requirements 

**I-20 calculation**  
**Amount**  
Tuition & fees  
**$24,192**  
Living expenses  
**$27,728**  
**Total funds required**  
**$51,920**

title: Anyone else received an OGS warning about taking an online certificate while on OPT?
content:
I’m on F-1 OPT/cap-gap, and my H-1B starts October 1. I’ve been taking a part-time online graduate certificate at Northeastern for about 1.5 years. Before enrolling, I spoke with OGS and my immigration attorney, and I was told it shouldn’t be an issue since it’s online, non-degree, and doesn’t provide F-1 status.

Yesterday, OGS suddenly told me that it could affect my OPT and asked me to withdraw from the program and both courses.

Has anyone dealt with something similar? What happened after you withdrew? Did it affect your OPT, cap-gap, or H-1B?

title: How will this DHS memo affect co-op at Northeastern?
content: This is a UC Berkeley International Office (BIO) notice dated August 13, 2026, informing students that an ICE guidance memo received August 12 narrows CPT authorization to cases where the internship is required for all students to earn the degree. As a result, BIO is temporarily suspending all "Course Credit CPT" applications (integral to the program but not a degree requirement) while continuing to process "Degree-Requirement" CPT as normal. The office says it is consulting legal counsel and notes possible legal challenges that could allow course-credit CPT processing to resume.

comments.body: International students you will now require a breathing license, approved by DHS.

ETA: for international students who require CPT authorization to work off campus.

Here’s the memo from ICE to DSOs across the US: https://www.ice.gov/doclib/sevis/pdf/bcm260801.pdf

Northeastern’s current OGS CPT policy already describes CPT as experiential learning that is “necessary and integral, or required” as part of an academic program. It specifically says CPT authorization is required for every co-op/internship/etc.  

And Northeastern explicitly says international students can participate in co-op with CPT authorization.  

So, at least on the face of the current Northeastern policy:

ICE’s new memo doesn’t contradict Northeastern’s co-op system.
